title: Google rolls out new search homepage with AI chat history and no search button
gist: Google is rolling out a redesigned desktop search homepage that removes the Google Search button, adds AI buttons (image generation, file analysis, Gemini brainstorming) and a sidebar of recent AI Mode threads. Author Ryan Whitwam reads it as a signal that traditional search is being de-emphasized and AI Mode could eventually become the default.

insights.claim: Google is deploying a new desktop search homepage, confirmed by search VP Robby Stein after a successful test, that drops the dedicated Google Search button and adds AI buttons for image generation, file analysis and brainstorming with Gemini, while keeping 'I'm Feeling Lucky'.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Google is steering its highest-traffic surface toward Gemini engagement, a key metric for its AI monetization.
insights.locator: Google search VP Robby Stein confirmed on X

insights.claim: The removed search button was likely rarely used because autocomplete suggestions covered it, so most users press Enter or click a suggestion, making the functional loss minimal.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: The change is low-risk for usage but symbolically important for product direction.
insights.locator: The search button has obviously been

insights.claim: Logged-in users get an expandable left sidebar of recent AI Mode search threads on the homepage and results page, which Stein said made a 'big difference' in how people progressed on searches.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Persistent AI conversation history raises engagement and switching costs versus rival chatbots.
insights.quote: simpler way to pick up where you left off
insights.locator: The other big change brings your recent AI conversations

insights.claim: Ryan Whitwam argues the redesign shows Google's priorities: AI features get prominent buttons and a full sidebar while traditional search is increasingly de-emphasized.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Shift toward AI answers threatens click-through to publishers and may change how Google monetizes search ads.
insights.locator: This change says more about Google’s priorities

insights.claim: Whitwam predicts a day may come when AI Mode takes over Google search completely, forcing users to manually select old-fashioned search, and says Google is inching in that direction.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Watch for AI Mode becoming the default as a major inflection for search advertising and SEO-dependent businesses.
insights.quote: There may come a day when AI Mode takes over completely
insights.locator: This change says more about Google’s priorities
